subject: GPU supply-chain and onboarding timeline for Q3 Dedicated Capacity
messages:
From: John Smith <john.smith@enterprise.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity timeline and vendor details for planned Q3 onboard

Rachel / Marcus,

We are lining up our vendor approvals and need to lock the procurement timeline for Redwood Dedicated capacity for Q3 onboarding (target: intake week of 2027-07-11). Can you share: 

- Estimated GPU count and instance profile you expect us to reserve (RPS and peak tokens included)
- Typical lead times you see for OEM hardware procurement vs. cloud reserved capacity (we need to present options to our procurement committee)
- Any vendor contacts or quote stubs we can include in our packet

I've attached our high-level capacity requirements (RFI_capacity_requirements.xlsx).

Also: our legal team prefers a PO-based path rather than commitment contracts up front — if that changes timelines please flag.

Thanks,
John Smith
Head of Platform
Enterprise AI
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@enterprise.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline and vendor details for planned Q3 onboard

John — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping Marcus (procurement/ops) and Karthik (sales) to align on sizing + lead times. Quick summary from our side based on the RFI and your traffic profile: 

- Recommended initial footprint: 32 x H100-equivalent GPU slots (configured as 8x8 pools) to meet target SLA for conversational latency at expected concurrency.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~2.8M tokens/hour with burst headroom of ~40% using our batching and KV caching.
- Mode options: OEM bare-metal procurement (on-prem or colo) OR cloud reserved capacity (GCP/AWS reserved instances or Dedicated hosts).

High-level lead-time expectations (prelim):
- OEM new-build lead time: 12–16 weeks from PO to delivery for H100-class systems (varies by region, customs).
- Cloud reserved capacity: 2–6 weeks for setup and testing but depends on quota approvals and provider availability in the target region.

Action items we recommend:
1) Marcus to request firm OEM quotes and confirm ETA windows with NV OEM sales.
2) Karthik to open a HubSpot deal task and flag procurement preference (PO vs commitment).
3) John to confirm any internal blackout dates or procurement freeze windows.

Attachment: initial-sizing-table.csv (basic pool layout + token assumptions).

I'll follow up once Marcus posts the vendor ETA and a fallback cloud timeline.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, John Smith <john.smith@enterprise.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline and vendor details for planned Q3 onboard

FYI — I reached out to NV OEM Sales (hw-sales@nv-oem.com) and consolidated preliminary lead times and quote terms. Key points below: 

- NV OEM response: Quote valid 30 days. Typical delivery 10–14 weeks after PO for standard H100 racks; 14–18 weeks for larger custom racks with additional NIC/HW integration. They noted 3–4 week lead on GPUs themselves if ordering out of stock.
- Pricing: nv-oem-quote-APR2027.pdf (attached stub) includes per-rack MSRP and recommended support SKUs.
- Customs & logistics: for our US West region the window usually skews toward the shorter end, but Q3 has heavy demand across hyperscalers and OEMs — plan on the mid-point (12–16 weeks).

Cloud reserved capacity alternative:
- I contacted Acme Cloud Sales to check large reserved pool availability in us-west-2; their response: capacity is available but requires commitment/PO and quota provisioning — provisioning completes in 7–21 days post-PO depending on quota.
- Cost tradeoff: cloud reserved instances cost ~1.6–2.2x of equivalent OEM hourly amortized cost but give faster time-to-service and less logistics overhead.

Risk & contingency plan:
- If PO is issued by 2027-04-28, OEM path likely still aligns with late-July onboarding.
- If procurement approval slips beyond May 10, fallback to hybrid model: 50% cloud reserved to cover initial weeks + OEM backlog for steady-state.

Requesting approvals from Sales/Customer on the above by 2027-04-20 so we can lock quotes / PO windows.

Attachments: nv-oem-quote-APR2027.pdf (quote stub).

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rachel_kim@redwood.com <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@enterprise.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline and vendor details for planned Q3 onboard

John — following up with a one-page decision plan to help procurement. TL;DR: if Enterprise AI can approve PO by 2027-04-28 we can proceed with OEM path and still hit late-July onboarding. If you need a softer commitment, we recommend the hybrid approach (cloud reserved first, OEM for steady-state).

Decision summary (for procurement packet):
- Option A (OEM): 32 H100-equivalent slots, PO to NV OEM; expected delivery 12–16 weeks -> target onboarding window: 2027-07-19 to 2027-07-26. Requires PO by 2027-04-28.
- Option B (Hybrid): 16 reserved cloud slots to start (available ~7–21 days after PO), OEM PO for remaining capacity; expected onboarding: phased, start early-July in-cloud then transition to Dedicated as racks arrive.

Next steps / owners: 
- John: confirm procurement preference and any constraints by 2027-04-26.
- Marcus: will submit finalized NV quote to you and prepare PO template.
- Karthik: will update HubSpot (DL-2027-0143) and provision billing contact.

DocuSign link for preliminary PO-ready paper: https://docusign.com/link/abc123 (placeholder — will send vendor-specific PO once you confirm).

If this timeline looks good I can prepare the one-page packet for your procurement committee.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference
